verdict: Rollout FAILED: the experiment ran, but val_bpb = 1.016521 did not improve on the current best 1.013025 by more than the required 0.0005 (lower is better).

insights_in_context.hint: Reducing MLP capacity to buy more steps made the model under-capacity, so the experiment should not have shrunk the 4x MLP expansion.
The bad choice was treating extra value-embedding tables as free capacity when they actually cost steps and undertrained within the fixed time budget.

Don't buy steps by cutting model capacity the way batch-halving did — GQA removed ~21% of params for only a ~4% speedup, so pick a capacity-neutral speedup or a small capacity/optimizer change instead.
Depth 10 at width 512 costs too many optimizer steps for this 5-minute budget, so stop pushing depth and try an optimizer or efficiency-neutral change instead.
The change itself was valid, but the chosen experiment was too low-prior to clear the required improvement threshold.
The prefetch code worked, but the step count only rose from 1844 to 1847, proving the dataloader was not the bottleneck, so a pure speedup could never produce the >0.0005 val_bpb gain you needed.

judge.summary: The agent read the current train.py and results.tsv, then chose a simple learning-rate schedule experiment: add a short linear warmup by changing WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.05, leaving WARMDOWN_RATIO at 0.7 and all other hyperparameters unchanged. It committed this one-line change and ran the experiment. The run completed successfully with val_bpb 1.016521, peak_vram_mb 25277.5, num_steps 1847, which is clearly worse than the current best 1.013025 and therefore failed to improve.
judge.feedback: The implementation itself appears correct: the run did not crash, the step count and token count are comparable to the best run, and the only semantic change was a 5% LR warmup. The first decisive mistake was the experimental choice in the edit step: introducing nonzero warmup delayed the high-LR phase in a schedule that was already working well with WARMUP_RATIO = 0.0, and the result shows this costs about 0.0035 val_bpb. There is no code bug to fix; the agent should have selected a different untried knob rather than adding warmup, or at least recognized that the existing no-warmup schedule was already near-optimal on the warmup side.
